headline: Nifty at two-month high, but US midterm count sets up a cautious open

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Wednesday, the fourth of November, and here's your Market Brief.

Three things matter most today. First, Dalal Street had a big day on Tuesday. The Sensex jumped more than twelve hundred points and the Nifty closed at a two-month high, as foreign investors bought heavily for a third straight session.

Second, America is counting votes in its midterm elections. Polls and prediction markets point to a strong Democratic showing, and US tech futures are sliding this morning. That means India is likely to open lower.

And third, the economy is sending mixed signals. Tax collections and factory activity look strong, but winter sowing is down by almost half because of poor rains, and that raises the risk of food inflation.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Let's start with the numbers. On Tuesday the Sensex gained about 1,225 points and the Nifty rose 370 points, or 1.6 percent, to close at 23,810. That was the fourth day of gains in a row, and it added roughly 4 lakh crore rupees to the value of listed companies. Falling crude prices, foreign buying and resilient earnings did the lifting, along with hopes of a change in long-term capital gains tax.

Banks led the way. The private bank index rose 2 percent, with HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank the biggest contributors. Each of them is up about 7 percent over the last five sessions. And Garden Reach Shipbuilders rose 9 percent, its best day in six months, after a defence order we'll come to shortly.

Now the money flows. Foreign institutional investors bought shares worth 6,836 crore rupees, their third straight day of buying. Domestic institutional investors sold 3,678 crore rupees for a third straight day.

The rupee firmed for a third session to settle at 94.75 to the dollar, and early this morning Moneycontrol had it stronger still, near 94.56.

For today, GIFT Nifty points to a softer start, around forty points lower. Analysts at Moneycontrol and HDFC Securities see the 23,900 to 24,000 zone, near the 200-day average, as the next hurdle, with support around 23,500 to 23,600.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
Now to the primary market. The payments company Razorpay has received the market regulator's approval for its IPO. Moneycontrol reports it could raise 500 to 600 million dollars at a valuation of about 5 billion dollars, with a listing likely in the January to March quarter.

SFC Environmental Technologies had a strong debut, closing its first day about 29 percent above its issue price of 330 rupees. And for M K Sons Fine Jewels, the grey market premium suggests a modest listing gain of around 6 percent over the issue price of 162 rupees.

On deals, the Defence Ministry signed contracts worth 53,866 crore rupees with Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Goa Shipyard for eight next-generation warships for the Navy. And Canara Bank and other lenders accepted a 522 crore rupee one-time settlement from Supreme Housing and Hospitality, recovering about 75 percent of dues of close to 700 crore rupees.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
Results season rolls on, so let's go sector by sector.

In banking, State Bank of India reported a 14 percent rise in net profit to 23,038 crore rupees for the September quarter. Loans grew 18 percent, and lower deposit costs and provisions helped. Brokerages are largely positive, Moneycontrol says, though some flag one-off gains behind the headline number. Among smaller lenders, Fusion Finance swung to a profit of about 86 crore rupees from a loss a year ago, and its shares jumped nearly 16 percent. Utkarsh Small Finance Bank went the other way, with a loss of 70 crore rupees, its sixth losing quarter in a row.

The market infrastructure names had a strong showing. The National Stock Exchange, in its first results since listing, posted a 23 percent rise in profit to 2,578 crore rupees. MCX did even better, with profit up 130 percent to about 455 crore rupees and revenue more than doubling.

In consumer goods, Marico raised its margin outlook for this financial year after strong growth in foods and premium personal care, helped by lower input costs. Bata India's profit rose 30 percent to about 18 crore rupees, on revenue of 862 crore rupees.

In technology, Happiest Minds grew profit 15 percent and revenue about 12 percent, but said growth was below its own target as key deals slipped and clients took longer to decide on artificial intelligence spending.

Today, Apollo Hospitals, BSE, Dabur, Nykaa, Lenskart, Physicswallah and Afcons are among those reporting. Bharti Airtel's numbers are also awaited, and Business Standard says brokerages expect revenue growth of 14 to 15 percent.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Now to the economy, and first the good news. Gross collections of the goods and services tax rose 23 percent in October to about 2.3 lakh crore rupees, the fastest growth in over four years. Revenue from imports surged 42 percent, and net collections rose about 26 percent to 2.03 lakh crore rupees. Factory activity stayed firmly in expansion, with the manufacturing purchasing managers' index at 54.7, slightly below September. Export orders grew at their fastest pace in six months.

On the other side, the countryside is under strain. The area sown with winter crops is down 46 percent from last year, at 37.6 lakh hectares, after a 48 percent rainfall shortfall in October. And Gaurav Moda of EY says the jump in crude from 60 to 65 dollars a barrel to 90 to 95 dollars could add up to one percentage point to inflation.

The Reserve Bank is soaking up spare cash. Banking system liquidity is in surplus by close to 2 lakh crore rupees. But at a 50,000 crore rupee reverse repo auction, banks offered only 23,905 crore rupees. Another auction of the same size is due today.

On tax, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said she will consider investors' concerns about how equity gains are taxed. SBI Research has proposed scrapping long-term capital gains tax on shares held for over three years, with a 2 lakh rupee exemption, paid for partly by a 50 percent increase in the securities transaction tax. It puts the cost at 40,000 to 50,000 crore rupees.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, all eyes are on the US midterm count. Prediction market Polymarket gave the Democrats about a 95 percent chance of winning the House, and as results trickle in, Nasdaq futures are down between one and two percent. On Tuesday itself, Wall Street was mixed. The Dow slipped 0.4 percent, while the S&P 500 rose 0.4 percent and the Nasdaq 0.8 percent, as chip stocks bounced and AMD jumped 8 percent.

Oil is edging down. Brent is around 103 dollars a barrel, as traders wait for the US vote and for progress in US and Iran peace talks. Qatar says both sides are studying fresh mediator proposals.

segments.title: Stories you're following
segments.script: An update on the India and US trade deal you're following. On Tuesday, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said India has never allowed imports of genetically modified products and never will, and that dairy has not been opened up in any trade agreement. Access for American dairy is one of the open questions in the deal, so that is a clear marker of India's position, just as Americans went to the polls.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Finally, your money, with the festive season under way.

Gold and silver have had a rough patch. All gold and silver exchange traded funds lost money in October for a second month running, with silver funds down about 17 percent on average. Inflows into gold funds slowed to about 3,300 crore rupees, from 4,450 crore in September, partly because fund houses paused fresh money into gold fund-of-funds on the regulator's direction. If you're weighing physical gold against a gold fund this Dhanteras, note the tax difference Mint points out. Gold funds qualify for long-term capital gains treatment after 12 months, while physical gold needs 24.

There's a proposal worth tracking too. The market regulator has recommended that switching between mutual fund schemes be made free of capital gains tax, if the units were held for more than a year.

A few changes to note. Punjab National Bank and Canara Bank have revised fixed deposit rates on some tenures from the first and second of November. And the insurance regulator will bring in a four-tier structure for car and two-wheeler insurance from the fifteenth of December.

One tax ruling for the professionals listening. The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal deleted an addition of 8.66 crore rupees against a woman whose computer held records of cash transactions found in a search. It held that the spending belonged to a real estate company, not to her.

And a word of caution. The Economic Times counts at least 63 stocks worth over 1,000 crore rupees that have lost more than half their value since last Diwali, some by as much as 96 percent.

That's the brief. Today, watch the US midterm results and how foreign investors react, whether the Nifty can clear 23,900, results from Apollo Hospitals, BSE and Dabur, and the Reserve Bank's second reverse repo auction. Have a good Wednesday.
